name: Bahrain

campaign_state.basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Bahrain were reported in 2026. No end to the wider war is reported, so the classification is uncertain, and uncertain is treated as active.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on the date checked. A search that returns no recent report does not show that none occurred. Iteration 20 added four conflict-level searches (the wider war, the Gulf states as a group, Iraq). None reported an end of the war, and renewed hostilities were reported in the autumn of 2026. No facility was looked up.

no_index_reason: Only the Russia-theatre system has a disruption index. Its weights and recovery assumptions were designed for that theatre and are not transferred to other countries, so this page shows reported disruptions and national energy context instead. No index is not a zero.

sectors.reason: The official refining series describe a single refinery, so a sector score would be one facility's status under another name. Annual national throughput and output are shown as context only.
sectors.label: Refining

sectors.reason: National installed capacity is published (IRENA), but the utility's station list was not read and its series covers public supply only, about half of national generation. With this few stations a governorate share would identify a station.
sectors.label: Electric generation

sectors.reason: No inventory was read and none should be built: a substation-level picture of a grid this small is outside the scope boundary.
sectors.label: Transmission burden

sectors.reason: No public capacity inventory was read, and building one would centre on import and export routing, which is out of scope.
sectors.label: Oil logistics & export

sectors.reason: National production is published annually and shown as context. Processing sits with a single operating group, so a score would be that group's facility status; LNG and storage are not yet researched.
sectors.label: Gas

sectors.reason: Not applicable: IRENA reports coal at 0% of Bahrain's total energy supply (2022) and no coal in power generation. The sector does not exist here, which is different from unknown.
sectors.label: Coal

reporting_environment_text: Operators and authorities do not publish event-level outage reports. Events come from media and company statements, so most smaller disruptions will not appear.
reporting_note: No operator, authority or regulator page reached publishes event-level outage or incident reports. Incidents become public through official statements carried by the state news agency and repeated by the domestic press, so most smaller disruptions will not appear and the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: Bahrain has 4 governorates today (Capital, Muharraq, Northern, Southern). Natural Earth draws 5, with their pre-2014 shapes, because it still includes the Central governorate that was abolished in 2014. Every record in this system is published at country level, so no governorate is ever shaded for an event. A blank map means records are not placed, not that nothing happened.

rulings.note: Capital governorate, drawn with its pre-2014 extent. The governorate is larger today (38 square km in 2012, 78 in 2015 in the official area series), so a place in today's Capital governorate may lie outside this shape.
Southern governorate, drawn as Natural Earth has it, from before the 2014 redivision; whether its extent changed then was not verified. Includes the Hawar Islands as Natural Earth draws them.

Central governorate: abolished in 2014, when the governorates were redivided into four (Survey and Land Registration Bureau, Area by Governorate). Drawn because Natural Earth still carries it; never assigned an event and never given an event count. An event that a source locates in this area is recorded at country level, not moved to a neighbouring unit.
Northern governorate, drawn as Natural Earth has it, from before the 2014 redivision; whether its extent changed then was not verified.

precision_policy.reason: Bahrain is about 780 square kilometres with a handful of energy facilities, and the map source still draws the five governorates that were replaced by four in 2014. A governorate would either identify the facility or place an event in a shape that no longer exists, so every record is the country's. Attacks and sabotage also carry no facility or operator.

refinery.basis: BH_SOURCE_AUDIT: the national refining series describes a single refinery.

lng_terminal.basis: The lead's reading of public reporting (iteration 20): one LNG import terminal. Not yet confirmed in the source audit; an entry here can only hold a record, never publish one.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

campaigns.name: Attacks on Bahraini energy facilities, 2026
campaigns.status_basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Bahrain were reported in 2026. No end to the wider war is reported, so the classification is uncertain, and uncertain is treated as active.

release_rule.text: Facility-specific restart, recovery or operating status for a record in a campaign is published only once the campaign is recorded as ended and 30 days have passed. While it is active the event itself is published; its facility status is not.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Bahrain source-audit lane (iteration 19, Wave A). CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read from the cited page or file in this session; vintages differ (2022-2025) and are stated per row, so the rows must not be combined into one 'current' picture. Bases differ by source: national totals from IRENA; annual series from the Ministry of Oil and Environment and the Electricity and Water Authority through data.gov.bh, extracted 2026-11-11 under the Bahrain Open Government Data License v1.1; sums and selections are this project's own and are not attributed to the iGA or the publishing entity. No refining or generating capacity by facility is recorded, and no refining or gas series later than 2025 is carried: the refining series describes a single refinery, so a later figure would be one facility's operating level. Crude-import and crude-origin series exist on the portal and are deliberately not carried. See docs/countries/BH_SOURCE_AUDIT.md. 3 figures newer than 2024 are withheld while the campaign policy applies.

metrics.basis: country total; gas 89%, oil 11%, coal and others 0%, renewables 0% (713 TJ), no nuclear. Supply, not production
country total (non-renewable 37,429; renewable 94). About twice the Electricity and Water Authority's own station series for the same year, which covers public supply only
country total installed capacity as IRENA reports it (non-renewable 9,885; renewable 69). Whether and how it includes generation outside the public utility is not stated on the page

significance: Natural gas made up 89% of Bahrain's total energy supply in 2022 and oil 11%, with coal at 0% and renewables under 1% (IRENA).
Almost all electricity is generated from non-renewable sources: 37,429 of 37,523 GWh in 2023 (IRENA).

Households took 48% of the electricity supplied by the Electricity and Water Authority in 2025, commercial users 33% and industry 19% (shares computed by this project from the authority's published sector figures).
Bahrain publishes annual national series for crude oil, gas, refining and electricity under an open government data licence (data.gov.bh).

source_health.origin_rule: An origin is a wire service the citation names, else the website it sits on. Wikipedia and content aggregators are discovery aids and count as no origin. Republication a record does not name cannot be seen, so this can undercount independence but not overstate it.
source_health.first_party_excludes: Wikipedia, whatever role a record gives it
source_health.note: Describes the citations of the published events in this country. Not opened and not recorded are different: a researcher who did not record whether a source was opened is not evidence that it was not. Nothing here is comparable across countries and nothing here enters a number.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: The citations of this system have not been link-checked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
